newsitem.title: MEXICO: Anchor Glass sold by Vitro SA, files bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: Anchor Glass sold by Vitro SA, files bankruptcy.

text.p: Mexican glass manufacturer Vitro S.A. said Friday that its U.S. subsidiary, Anchor Glass Container Corp., has agreed to sell its assets to Ball-Foster Glass Container Co. L.L.C. of Muncie, Indiana for $365 million in cash and the assumption of certain liabilities.
Vitro also said that Tampa, Fla.-based Anchor, the third largest U.S. glass container company, filed for bankruptcy in order to assure continued operation through the closing of the sale.
In May, Vitro had said that it wanted to sell business units that failed to meet a minimum return requirement of 14 percent. The company later announced that it was seeking to sell Anchor.
On Friday, Vitro informed Anchor that it would no longer support the unit's liquidity needs.
The company said Anchor suffered from continuing contraction of U.S. glass container demand, unfavourable operating results and continuing liquidity needs.
In court papers filed with the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Wilmington, Del., Anchor listed assets of $1.2 billion and liabilities of $951.1 million.
Among the largest unsecured creditors are Chase Manhattan Bank with $200 million in notes due, and Bank of America, with $100 million in notes due, court papers said.
Anchor said that it has obtained the consent of senior secured lenders for a $130 million line of credit.
The sale of the unit is subject to the signing of a definitive agreement by Anchor, Ball-Foster and Vitro.
